The council normally elects by thirds, with all-out elections used where new boundaries required a full council election, as happened in 2018 before returning to elections by thirds [d67582869s1p0]. There has been local debate and campaigning over creating a directly elected mayor for Newcastle, with local party groups indicating they would stand if the position were created [d34346305s9p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What statutory relationships and mechanisms exist between Newcastle City Council and regional/national bodies (e.g., county-level authorities, central government)?
sub_answers.text: From 1974 Newcastle was a district within the Tyne and Wear metropolitan county and initially received county-level services from Tyne and Wear County Council [d67582869s1p0]. The abolition of the metropolitan county council in 1986 transferred county-level functions to the metropolitan districts themselves, consolidating powers at the borough level [d67582869s1p0]. Some services are provided through joint arrangements with other Tyne and Wear councils and through combined authorities such as the North of Tyne Combined Authority created in 2018 and the North East Mayoral Combined Authority established in 2024, which oversee strategic functions and are chaired by directly elected regional mayors [d41381311s2p0][d67582869s1p0].
